entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Sets a deleted_at timestamp on the user row and commits; it issues no delete.

stores.name: users

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: The column the close_account route writes and the purge job filters on.

erasure.note: The route only stamps deleted_at; the Celery beat task purge_closed_accounts selects users whose deleted_at is older than 30 days and calls session.delete on each row.

stores.note: The user table, written by the account and profile routes.

stores.name: invoices

erasure.note: The User.invoices relationship carries no cascade string, so the ORM delete in the purge job does not propagate; the only delete path is the database-level ondelete="CASCADE", and the SQLite URL in config.py comes with no PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON listener anywhere in the repository, so the source does not settle whether the child rows go.

stores.note: Invoice rows joined to a user by user_id; a comment on the reference column says the purge job does not touch this table.

stores.name: nightly_backup

fields.name: email
fields.note: Named in DUMP_COLUMNS and read off each row with getattr before being written to the JSON file.

fields.name: reference
fields.note: The invoice reference column, copied into the same dump.

erasure.note: The module declares a 35-day backup retention and a nightly cron string, but no code in this repository reads BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS or removes the dump file; dump_database rewrites nightly_backup.json in place.

stores.note: A JSON dump of selected user and invoice columns written to a file on disk.

retention.criteria: no job in the repository selects rows from this table for deletion
